summary: The note describes how the permanent shift to remote work has widened the attack surface and is forcing endpoint security to evolve beyond perimeter-based defenses. It covers expected trends: behavior-based security, AI and machine learning, Zero Trust, more advanced EDR, device management policies, SASE, biometric authentication, and insurer-mandated security requirements. Several named experts are quoted in support of these trends.
one_line: Overview of emerging endpoint security strategies for remote work, including AI, Zero Trust, EDR, SASE, biometrics, and insurance-driven requirements.
key_facts: Remote work has evolved from a temporary measure to a permanent fixture, broadening the attack surface for organizations.
Traditional perimeter-based security is no longer adequate because attackers exploit personal devices and unsecured networks.

Maria Gonzalez, a leading cybersecurity analyst interviewed on October 12, 2023, said "Security solutions that can adapt in real-time to how a device is being used, and potentially misused, will become invaluable."

Robert Smith, CTO of SecureTech Innovations, said at the CyberSecurity Summit on November 3rd, 2023 that tomorrow's endpoint security will use AI to spot irregularities and threats before they cause harm.
AI systems are being trained to recognize baseline behaviors and react to deviations that signal possible cyber threats.
The Zero Trust model follows 'never trust, always verify', treating every access request as if it originates from an open network.
Owen Jacobs, a cybersecurity consultant interviewed on September 18, 2023, called Zero Trust "not just a technology but a mindset" that must be ingrained in company culture.
By 2024 and beyond, EDR solutions will likely serve as the central nervous system of endpoint security, using vast datasets to detect anomalies and automate responses.
CyberSafe Solutions is cited as creating device management policies that balance security with user convenience.
Sara Burns, speaking at the annual NetSec conference on December 10, 2023, described SASE as the evolution of network architecture offering scalable, unified security for a distributed workforce.
SASE converges network and security services into a single, cloud-delivered service model.
Biometric authentication such as fingerprint scanners, facial recognition, and behavioral biometrics is predicted to become commonplace for protecting remote devices.
Insurers are starting to mandate more stringent endpoint security measures as a prerequisite for cybersecurity insurance coverage.
